extracted.intended_audience: scientists and engineers (especially those with little media experience) seeking guidance on engaging with the news media in the UK
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and institutional standards for scientists and engineers on engaging with journalists and the news media, including training opportunities, publications, and conflict-of-interest disclosure when speaking to press or taking part in briefings.

rubrics_metrics.name: SMC goal: ensure the best experts are heard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Science Media Centre’s goal is to make sure that the best experts are heard by the public when science/engineering is in the news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SMC team provides support for experts and maintains a database of experts; it has strong connections with UK universities, industry, learned societies and scientific/engineering institutions to help identify and promote appropriate spokespeople.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for engagement, particularly on controversial subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: The SMC provides support for scientists and engineers to engage with the media when their area hits the headlines, particularly on controversial subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SMC offers tailored help to scientists dealing with controversial or high-profile stories, signaling that extra preparation and institutional support are appropriate in these contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use off-the-record brainstorms to plan communication on controversial topics
rubrics_metrics.description: The SMC runs off-the-record brainstorms to discuss how the scientific community can effectively and accurately communicate findings on a controversial subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These sessions are intended to enable candid discussion about messaging and strategy before public engagement; participating can help align community responses and improve accuracy of public communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend subject-focused advisory sessions ahead of major stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Occasionally the SMC will run subject-focused advisory sessions in anticipation of big controversial stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively attending advisory sessions prior to a predicted major story is recommended to prepare messaging, anticipate media angles, and coordinate expert responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction to the News Media events for inexperienced scientists
rubrics_metrics.description: For scientists and engineers with little media experience, the Centre offers free places at its hugely popular ‘Introduction to the News Media’ events which give a flavour of what media work involves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These sessions focus on subjects likely to hit the headlines and explain the reality of today's news landscape; they are recommended for early-career or media-new scientists and include sign-up information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted communications workshops (e.g., Impact: Women scientists in the media)
rubrics_metrics.description: SMC collaborated to run communications workshops, for women scientists at a post-doctoral level (or equivalent) or above, working in areas of science of interest to the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek out targeted workshops (by career stage or demographic) when available; such programmes may be sponsored or run in partnership with other organisations and focus on practical media engagement skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use SMC publications/guides to prepare concise interview answers
rubrics_metrics.description: Working with journalists, press officers and media-experienced scientists, the SMC has produced guides that advise experts on effective ways of answering complex questions in a two minute news interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult SMC guides when preparing for short broadcast interviews; specific guides address topics such as risk, animal research, peer review and uncertainty and are produced to help experts communicate complex issues succinctly and clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare interests when briefing or supplying quotes (register of interests policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: For experts taking part in a briefing or supplying a quote we have produced a guidance note regarding SMC policy on declaring interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the SMC guidance note on declaring interests/conflicts of interest when participating in briefings or providing quotes to ensure transparency; consult the register-of-interests policy for required disclosures.
